before.label: Clifford Geertz
before.description: Culture consists of publicly interpretable meanings. Thick description reconstructs the contexts that make actions intelligible; it is more than adding descriptive detail.
before.representative_figures_and_works: The Interpretation of Cultures (1973). Weber, Wittgenstein, and Ryle are explicit interlocutors; the approach becomes influential in cultural history.

after.label: Clifford Geertz
after.description: Culture consists of publicly interpretable meanings. Thick description reconstructs the contexts that make actions intelligible; it is more than adding descriptive detail. “Deep Play” (1972) reads cockfighting through status and symbolic action; Negara (1980) examines ritual and political authority in nineteenth-century Bali. These are his interpretations, with their empirical reach open to debate.
after.representative_figures_and_works: The Interpretation of Cultures (1973). Weber, Wittgenstein, and Ryle are explicit interlocutors; the approach becomes influential in cultural history.
after.scope_note: Thick description interprets public, situated meanings and constrains interpretations through evidence. Hunt’s adaptation is a specific historical reception; Asad’s religion-category criticism targets a particular argument. These readings do not summarize every Indonesian or Moroccan study or establish a uniform Geertzian cultural history.

before.label: Structural linguistics

before.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
before.description: Analyzes kinship and myth through underlying relations, oppositions, and transformations. Structural explanation differs from Geertz’s interpretation of situated public meanings.
before.representative_figures_and_works: The Elementary Structures of Kinship (1949); Structural Anthropology (1958). Engagements with history vary; structuralism is not simply any interest in social structures.

after.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
after.description: Analyzes kinship and myth through underlying relations, oppositions, and transformations. Structural explanation differs from Geertz’s interpretation of situated public meanings. The Savage Mind (1962; English 1966) uses bricolage to examine recombination of available signs and materials, while rejecting an evolutionary ranking of mythical and scientific thought.
after.representative_figures_and_works: The Elementary Structures of Kinship (1949); Structural Anthropology (1958). Engagements with history vary; structuralism is not simply any interest in social structures.
after.scope_note: Relational models are distinct from simply studying social structure. The historical and linguistic chapters connect evidence and formal explanation without identifying anthropology with history. English 1963 passages are from the revised 1958 collection. Later adaptations by Hall and Hebdige, and Derrida’s criticism, are separately evidenced; the Braudel and Lacan exchanges still need stronger passage checks.

anthropology.people: Expanded the seven-person selection to twenty-eight, distinguishing fieldwork, functional analysis, gifts, historical anthropology, interpretation, feminist inquiry and research authority. Added Malinowski, Radcliffe-Brown, Evans-Pritchard, Mauss, Benedict, Mead, Turner, Sahlins, Cohn, Asad, Clifford, Marcus, Fabian, Behar, Gordon, Hurston, Fei and Leach; reused Lévi-Strauss, Wolf and Douglas. Buck and the Yukon collaboration retain distinct positions. This is a sociocultural teaching selection, not the whole anthropological discipline.
anthropology.works_and_arguments: Filled all three baseline anthropology gaps with Tylor’s Primitive Culture, Frazer’s Golden Bough and Boas’s 1896 comparative-method essay, recording consulted editions separately. Primary readings clarify comparison, historical comparability, daily observation, public meaning, temporal distancing and categories of religion. Added dated contextual readings for every new selection, distinguishing bibliographic entries from primary argument checks. Jakobson’s neighboring blank is also filled from Lévi-Strauss’s named references.
anthropology.internal_distinctions: Seventeen approaches retain the four existing IDs and distinguish overlapping research programmes. Functionalism differs from structural analysis, fieldwork from a universal theory, and historical anthropology from a homogeneous return to history. Feminist canon revision, Chinese village inquiry, collaboration and temporal criticism remain visible rather than being folded into a single interpretive turn. Benedict/Mead readings carry different evidentiary limits.
anthropology.incoming_connections: Added Radcliffe-Brown’s explicit Durkheim borrowing and a situated feminist-history contribution; Geertz’s internal conceptual criticism and Wilson’s earlier research-authority critique have distinct targets. Fei’s primary retrospective identifies local initiatives, Firth and Malinowski without deriving all Chinese research from an imported programme. Other exchange mechanisms appear in contextual rosters rather than fabricated institution-wide descent arrows.
anthropology.outgoing_connections: Added Asad’s specific criticism of Geertz’s religion argument. Strengthened the cultural-history contribution with Hunt’s named reception and reconciled Vansina’s note with its actual primary check. Reviewed the existing Medick/Cohn, Polanyi, consumption, Cronon, Mintz/Price, Rosaldo and Laboratory Life routes: these are separate projects, with their previously recorded limits retained. The anthropology/microhistory comparison and contribution coexist deliberately.
anthropology.evidence_and_interpretation: Primary excerpts, visual scan readings, secondary scholarship, publisher descriptions and metadata are labeled separately. Tylor 1920, Frazer 1894, Geertz 2005, Lévi-Strauss 1963 and later translations/reissues are not silently substituted for original dates. Hirsch’s retrospective supports particular Evans-Pritchard/Leach distinctions, not every statement in its broad narrative. No inherited endpoints or classifications changed; original representative prose and the New Left/Thompson correction survive.

levistrauss.people: Individual entry, so no group roster is required. Named resources now distinguish Durkheim, Mauss, Jakobson, Trubetzkoy and Febvre; Hall, Hebdige and Derrida remain separate recipients or critics. Added Lévi-Strauss to anthropology’s contextual roster without a new full node or duplicate identity. Fei and other anthropological programmes are not subsumed under structuralism.
levistrauss.works_and_arguments: Retained Elementary Structures of Kinship (1949) and Structural Anthropology (1958) in original representative prose. Read selected historical/linguistic chapters of the 1963 English collection and the opening/bricolage passages of The Savage Mind (1962; English 1966). The account now links relational models, historical evidence and recombination rather than merely naming structures. Full kinship and myth corpora remain outside this passage review.
levistrauss.internal_distinctions: Distinguished kinship/myth relations, phonological analogy, historical reconstruction and bricolage. The primary chapter qualifies transfer from linguistics; The Savage Mind rejects a ladder from mythical to scientific thought. The individual entry uses description/scope rather than group strands. Its historical method is not synonymous with Geertz’s situated interpretation.
levistrauss.incoming_connections: Strengthened edge_007 with named Jakobson/Trubetzkoy references and edge_012 with the Durkheim dedication and Mauss opening. Added Febvre’s named history-of-unbelief reception from Structural Anthropology p. 23. Derrida’s nature/culture and bricolage criticism gains a primary English transcription check while preserving Lévi-Strauss’s own conceptual questioning. No direct Saussure collaboration asserted.
levistrauss.outgoing_connections: Retained the Hall/Hebdige contribution supported by their primary passages. Reviewed Lacan and Braudel routes; the Braudel evidence note now explicitly says that its p. 729 check does not substantiate the structural-anthropology exchange. The new primary history chapter supplies context but cannot stand in for recipient evidence. Targeted reception gaps remain queued.
levistrauss.evidence_and_interpretation: Sources distinguish 1958 collection, 1963 English text, 1962/1966 Savage Mind and reformatted PDF pagination. Bibliography notes verify Jakobson work identities, not full reading of those works. The familiar sentence attributed to Marx by Lévi-Strauss was not reproduced as an authenticated Marx quotation. Existing IDs, original prose, directions and the qualified cultural-studies edge remain intact.

geertz.people: Individual entry, without an invented roster or school membership. Weber, Ryle and Wittgenstein are verified as named interlocutors; Hunt is a documented historical recipient and Asad a specific critic. The anthropology context now distinguishes Geertz from structural, functional, historical and feminist programmes. No claim that all cultural historians descend from him.
geertz.works_and_arguments: Read Thick Description pp. 3–13 and 25–30 in the Stanford transcription: public meaning, contextual differentiation, theory within cases and evidentiary constraints. Added Deep Play (1972), with selected passages from the identified 2005 reprint, and Negara (1980), supported by a publisher retrospective. Status drama and political ritual illustrate distinct projects; empirical generalizations are not certified by these readings.
geertz.internal_distinctions: Distinguished thick description from descriptive abundance and private mental contents; distinguished a methodological essay from cockfight interpretation and the nineteenth-century theatre-state argument. Asad’s historical category critique does not establish that Geertz disregarded all history or power. Sources and scope note retain the limits of a selective individual review.
geertz.incoming_connections: Strengthened the three explicit influence notes with exact Thick Description passages. Added Asad’s contribution from within anthropology as a directed critique: primary pp. 27–32 use the 1966 religion essay as a starting point, expressly not a review of all Geertz. The existing undirected disciplinary-setting comparison remains separate.
geertz.outgoing_connections: Strengthened cultural-history reception through Hunt’s 1984 p. 87 and retained its distinct political-history edge. The Negara description supports his project and argument, not proof that force was absent in Bali. New claims preserve contestability, contextual specificity and the original representative prose.
